title: Total Cost of Studying in Australia for Indian Students (2026–2027 Breakdown)

runs.t: Planning to study in Australia? Before choosing a university, understand how much you may need for tuition fees, accommodation, food, transport and other expenses. Your total budget depends on your course, university, city and lifestyle. This guide explains the main costs Indian students should include when planning for 2026–2027.

There is no single total cost for studying in Australia. Start with the exact course tuition fee, add a realistic city-and-accommodation budget, then include visa, OSHC, travel and set-up costs. The student visa living-cost figure is a financial-capacity benchmark, not a promise that it will cover every student’s actual expenses.

sections.title: What makes up the cost of studying in Australia?

runs.t: Build your budget around four main cost groups:
Tuition fees – the amount charged by your university or education provider for the course.
Living expenses – accommodation, groceries, transport, utilities, phone and personal spending.
Visa and health insurance – the Student visa (subclass 500) application charge and Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC), where required.
Pre-arrival and study costs – English tests, flights, books, equipment, deposits and initial household items.
For a multi-year degree, calculate the full course cost. Do not assume the first-year tuition fee will remain unchanged throughout your studies.

sections.title: Tuition fees: compare the actual course, not just the subject

runs.t: Tuition fees vary by institution, course, study level, credit load and year of commencement. Even programmes within the same subject area can have different fees.
The University of Sydney publishes indicative annual fees for international students. Its 2027 postgraduate coursework guide includes the following study-area ranges:

These are examples from one university, not Australia-wide averages. The university states that fees are indicative, are based on a full-time study load and can change annually. Always open the individual course page and confirm the fee for your intended start year.
Ask for the total tuition estimate for the full course duration, including the provider’s policy on annual fee increases and any additional course charges.

sections.title: Living expenses: plan for your actual city and lifestyle

runs.t: Your living costs depend on where you live, how far you travel to campus and whether you rent privately, share a house or choose managed student accommodation.

For Student visa financial-capacity purposes, the Department of Home Affairs currently lists AUD 29,710 as the 12-month living-cost amount for the primary student applicant. This is a visa benchmark. Study Australia cautions that actual living costs vary across Australia and may be much higher.
Include these categories in your personal budget:
Accommodation and bond – weekly rent, initial bond, advance rent and any utilities not included.
Food and groceries – estimate weekly groceries separately from eating out.
Transport – consider campus location, public transport access and concession eligibility.
Utilities and connectivity – electricity, gas, water, internet and mobile phone costs.
Personal and study expenses – clothing, medical gap costs, books, software, equipment and recreation.

sections.title: Does the city you choose change your budget?

runs.t: Yes. Rent, transport options and day-to-day costs differ between cities and suburbs. Compare the location of the campus, realistic travel times and accommodation options rather than relying on a simple “cheapest city” ranking.

rows.t: Compare rent close to campus with suburbs connected by public transport.
Check whether shared housing or student accommodation is practical for your campus.
Compare inner-city and suburban rent alongside commute costs.
Include the distance between accommodation, campus and essential services.
Compare available student housing and the transport route to campus.
Check the availability and cost of housing near your institution.

runs.t: Use the official Study Australia Cost of Living Calculator as a starting point. Its estimates are approximate and depend on the choices entered. Recheck the underlying data and assumptions when using it for a specific intake.

sections.title: Student visa, OSHC and other one-off costs

runs.t: Add pre-arrival and compliance costs separately so they are not overlooked.

rows.t: Home Affairs lists the charge from AUD 2,500 for the main applicant; concessions may apply in limited circumstances. Confirm the amount in the Visa Pricing Estimator before applying.
Generally required for student visa holders for the relevant period, subject to limited exemptions. Compare approved providers, cover dates and policy terms.
Depends on the test, location and provider. Check the current test fee directly.
Compare dates, baggage allowances, route and change conditions.
Allow for bond, advance rent, utilities, bedding and household essentials.
Books, software, equipment, uniforms or practical-course costs may apply.

sections.title: How much money do you need to show for an Australian Student visa?

runs.t: The Department of Home Affairs says applicants must show access to funds for travel, 12 months of course fees (or the relevant pro-rata amount), 12 months of living costs for themselves and accompanying family members, and school costs for school-age dependants where applicable.
The currently published 12-month living-cost amounts are:
Primary student applicant: AUD 29,710.
Partner accompanying the student: AUD 10,394.
Each dependent child: AUD 4,449.

blocks.title: Do not confuse these two budgets

runs.t: The visa financial-capacity calculation is not the same as the full cost of completing a degree. Plan for the entire course, possible annual fee increases, actual living expenses and emergencies.

Financial evidence requirements and accepted evidence can depend on the applicant’s circumstances and the applicable visa settings. Use the official Student visa page and Document Checklist Tool for the current instructions.

sections.title: How can Indian students manage the cost?

runs.t: Compare full-course fees.
Look at the complete course duration, annual fee changes, deposits and additional charges.
Check scholarship conditions.
Confirm eligibility, award value, renewal conditions, deadlines and whether the scholarship reduces tuition or provides a stipend.
Choose accommodation carefully.
Compare shared housing, managed student accommodation and private rentals, including utilities and commute costs.
Build a monthly budget.
Set realistic amounts for rent, food, transport, bills and personal expenses.
Prepare for the initial settlement period.
Keep funds for deposits, travel and first-month essentials before relying on any future income.
Do not rely on part-time work to finance tuition.
Work rights are subject to visa conditions and work availability is not guaranteed. Treat earnings as a possible contribution, not the foundation of your education funding.

sections.title: Example: building a two-year master's budget

runs.t: Use a transparent worked example rather than suggesting one fixed price for every student.

Assume a course has an annual tuition fee of AUD 40,000–55,000 and runs for two years. If fees did not increase, tuition would total AUD 80,000–110,000. Using the AUD 29,710 annual visa living-cost benchmark purely as a planning reference adds AUD 59,420 over two years.

rows.t: Living benchmark at AUD 29,710 per year

runs.t: This subtotal excludes visa charges, OSHC, flights, tests, course materials, initial accommodation costs, emergency funds and any annual tuition increase. The AUD 29,710 figure is a visa benchmark, not a claim that actual living expenses will be limited to that amount.

sections.title: Final checklist before accepting an offer

runs.t: Confirm the tuition fee for the exact course, campus and intake.
Calculate tuition for the full course duration and allow for annual increases.
Check scholarship value, eligibility and renewal conditions.
Estimate rent, bond, utilities, groceries and transport in the chosen city.
Confirm the current visa charge and financial-capacity evidence requirements.
Arrange OSHC for the required period and compare approved providers.
Budget for flights, tests, books, equipment and initial settlement.
Confirm how the course will be funded and keep an emergency buffer.
The strongest financial plan considers the entire study journey, not only the first semester or the minimum amount needed for a visa.

faq.q: How much does it cost to study in Australia for Indian students?

runs.t: There is no single fixed amount. Calculate the exact tuition fee for your course, then add realistic living expenses, visa charges, OSHC, travel and initial set-up costs. Fees and living costs vary by university, city and lifestyle.

faq.q: What is the minimum living-cost amount for an Australian Student visa?

runs.t: The Department of Home Affairs currently lists AUD 29,710 for 12 months for the primary student applicant. This is a financial-capacity figure for visa purposes, not a guaranteed estimate of actual living costs.

faq.q: Are tuition fees the same across Australian universities?

runs.t: No. Fees vary by institution, course, study level, credit load and year of entry. Check the official course page and request the full-course fee estimate from the university.

faq.q: Is OSHC compulsory for Indian students?

runs.t: Most Student visa holders must maintain adequate Overseas Student Health Cover for the required period. Limited exemptions apply to some circumstances or nationalities. Confirm the rule and policy dates with Home Affairs and the insurer.

faq.q: Can students pay Australian university fees in instalments?

runs.t: Many universities issue tuition invoices by semester or study period, but payment dates and arrangements vary. Follow the offer letter and the university’s official fee-payment instructions.

faq.q: Can part-time work pay for tuition and living expenses?

runs.t: Part-time work may contribute to everyday expenses, but work is not guaranteed and visa conditions apply. Students should arrange sufficient funds for tuition and living costs without depending on future employment.

faq.q: Are scholarships available for Indian students in Australia?

runs.t: Australian universities offer scholarships to eligible international students. Award values, eligibility, application processes and renewal conditions vary by institution and course.

faq.q: What should I budget before travelling to Australia?

runs.t: Include payments due before enrolment, visa charges, OSHC, flights, accommodation bond or deposit, initial rent and money for food, transport and essentials during the first weeks.
